title: Conversational AI for Relational Empathy in Informed Consent: A Prospective Three-Arm Randomized Controlled Study
summary: Before an examination, patients need clear information and an opportunity to discuss their questions and concerns. This study investigates whether a digital conversation assistant designed to respond empathetically helps patients feel understood and involved in decisions. 300 adults are randomly assigned to three equal groups: an empathetic digital assistant, a neutral and factual digital assistant, or a physician consultation alone. Both digital assistants provide the same information. All participants receive a physician-led discussion about the examination. Questionnaires assess participants’ experiences. Conversation times are measured, and physicians assess the conversation content and the medical histories collected.
conditions: All patients undergoing MRI or CT

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Scheduled or completed, clinically indicated CT or MRI examination.
Sufficient German language proficiency for interaction and questionnaire completion.
Written informed consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Cognitive or physical impairments preventing chatbot interaction or questionnaire completion.
Lack of capacity to provide informed consent.
Language barriers precluding study participation.
Urgent or emergency procedures for which the informed consent discussion may exceptionally be omitted.
Previous receipt of an identical informed consent discussion for the index examination.
Hospital employees, students or other individuals in a dependent relationship.
